strengths: The title screen states the dynasty premise in plain language before you press anything: 'Each life hands the next its name, its means, its reputation — and its secrets. Over the generations, a house takes shape.' No gaming vocabulary required.

The seenIntro hint fires within two seconds of your first life beginning and explains the passive time mechanic in one sentence: 'The years move on their own — pause any time with the ▮▮ below. Now and then, a moment will ask something of you.' A non-gamer doesn't need to figure this out.
The 'cannot be undone' framing on the title screen sets stakes before the first choice. You know it matters before it matters.

The dynasty breadcrumb — 'Everything this life gathers — its name, its means, its standing — will pass to the one who comes after.' — fires after two decisions in the first life. By the time you face your third choice you already know this life is building toward something.

The heir identity line ('You are no longer [name]. You are [name], their son/daughter — born into the world they left behind.') is the clearest possible handoff. There is no confusion about what has happened.
The pulse dot on the flow text and the age numeral breath animation together mean the screen never looks frozen to someone who doesn't know what a card is or when the next one comes.
The 'how things stand' button is visible with a border, opt-in, and gives a number-free prose readout. A curious newcomer can ask 'how am I doing?' without needing a stats screen.
Ambient whispers during quiet years fill the silence so a first-timer doesn't think the game has broken while waiting for the next event.

The transcripts confirm the writing is consistently strong across many lives — choices feel consequential and the prose around ordinary events ('Want has become a quiet, constant houseguest.') is atmospheric without being opaque.

improvements.what: Add a single sentence to the death modal priming 'what passes now' before 'Become [name]'
improvements.why: A first-timer who missed the seenDynasty breadcrumb (it fades after 13 seconds) may still be surprised at death — the title's dynasty premise is not restated between the breadcrumb and the heir screen. The heir identity line does good work, but a brief line on the death modal itself ('The life ends. What it gathered passes on.') would smooth the transition for the inattentive.

improvements.what: Stagger seenLog to decisions.length >= 3 instead of >= 2
improvements.why: seenLog and seenDynasty both fire at decisions.length >= 2, so the second choice can produce two orientation lines back-to-back. The dynasty breadcrumb is the priority; the log tap hint is lower stakes and having it appear one beat later would let the dynasty line breathe.

verdict: The round-8 changes don't touch the onboarding layer a first-timer sees, and that layer remains solid — dynasty hook on the title, 'cannot be undone' framing, the seenIntro hint, the first-life dynasty breadcrumb, and the heir identity line together give a non-gamer everything they need to understand what the game is and why it matters; I would recommend this to someone who reads.
